original_context_note:
Compared candidate 19 with target-selection.json/full_target and problem.md:45-122,123-646. spec.full_target preserves the selected string exactly. The ambient parameters T,gamma,R are unrestricted reals, with precisely the original three range assumptions H001-H003. Reality, mean zero, H^gamma membership, the norm-ball bound, positive integer L and tau=T/L<=tau0 remain explicit under the universal datum/step quantifiers in P; constants are chosen before those quantifiers, not after fixing a datum. No desired conclusion is an H. D001-D007 preserve the normalized 2*pi torus, Fourier/Sobolev conventions, Airy sign, mean projections and inverse derivative; D008 preserves every coefficient, product, Airy argument and endpoint sign of the supplied fixed update. D009 is proof-only. D010-D019 and D021 retain the covariance, four-frequency order, cubic remainder, normal forms, stage and exact residual formulas. D020 defines a solution convention rather than granting a solution: R001 constructs each solution from E001. Every D is a typed operator/formula/family with its displayed domain and binders; there is no existentially chosen global object or hidden construction guard. Polynomial-only R2 is extended by R005 before its L^2 use, and Interp is used with smooth paths until R012's fixed-timestep limit; it grants no endpoint or residual property before R007 proves them. All 21 definitions and their domain dependencies were read in the actual packets.
Primary sources were actually accessed and read: E001 is the specified 42-page arXiv:0910.1389v2 (23 October 2010), with the source equation, normalized homogeneous norms, integrated-solution definition, positive-order estimates, uniqueness/continuity and theta=0 comparison checked; the available arXiv version history was checked. E002-E005 are the exact cited 50-page Li-Wu author manuscript at the supplied PolyU URL, whose title, authors, unnormalized norms, complete Proposition 3.4, Lemma 7.2, product inequalities and exact step/remainder identities were checked. The publisher DOI metadata identifies the article; manuscript numbering was retained instead of silently adopting journal numbering. The unsuccessful Google/browser readback attempts remain recorded, but both actual cited originals are available, so no primary-source deferral or UNVERIFIED_PRIMARY assumption was used. Source records bind the PDF/text/access hashes and complete relevant statements; source fidelity remains subject to independent Audit A. E001's source sign and norm comparison are proved in R001; E002-E004's fixed normalization factors and the arbitrary-base stage bridge are proved in R002. The logarithmic convergence theorem is never an input.
The graph has 3 H, 5 external contracts, 11 internal outputs and P, with one producer per internal/target and no cycles; every non-H lies in P's backward AND closure. All original H are retained and actually used; none is unused. The constructor partition separates flow/source bridges, pointwise covariance geometry, dyadic summation, remainder extension, elementary products/normal forms, exact scheme connection, interpolation estimates, residuals, low/high stability, restarted bootstrap and density. R008 and R010 are the longer coherent tasks because their estimates share the same step/interval context; their exports supply every bound the next consumer needs. All needed calculations and limiting arguments of problem.md:105-646 are retained, including the zero-exponent local bound, resonances, both restarted endpoints, actual forcing calculation, partial steps, first-hit bootstrap and fixed-timestep finite-iteration limit. Section 5's finite numerical experiments and optional discussion are omitted because they are independent illustrations outside the selected theorem's analytic proof. In particular no global uniform L^2-ball rate at gamma=0 is claimed. All twelve own packets have been inspected; the unchanged R003/R004 read receipts were correctly retained from candidate 18. These are same-author closing checks, not Audit A verdicts.

output_notes.note: R001/S001-S003 establishes existence, uniqueness, C_t H^gamma, smooth-data compatibility and the common A(T,gamma,R) bound by the checked source, sign transformation and homogeneous norm comparison. The theta=0 two-flow estimate and finite-Fourier-sum limiting bound are exported explicitly; no producer-only fact is required by the later density argument.

R002/S001 exports both full normalized C estimates, all three negative slots, the sigma=0 endpoint and constant-input conditions. S002-S003 exports the product input regularities and both stage orders with correct exponents, epsilon=1/8 and the Airy-conjugation bridge to every a>=0; the whole constant dependence is stated.
R003/S001-S004 covers the zero-phase case, both phase ratios and tau-min bound, N1<=3N2, and both 3/N3 and 6/N3 pointwise majorants for every nonzero zero-sum quadruple, including ties.

R004/S001-S003 proves the absolute four-linear bound and restriction clause. The shell gain 2^(-(j3-j4)/2), three offsets, at most 24 orders and positive finite-sum supremum pass to infinite ell^2 inputs are all present.

R005/S001-S004 exports the explicit H^sigma->L^2 bound including sigma=0, every base time, arbitrary modulus-one restrictions and the continuous extension. The numerical-state clause explicitly has mean-zero w,f and delta<=1; its tau*(tau^gamma+delta) bound uses only the numerical L^2 norm, not H^gamma.

R006/S001-S003 supplies the uniform Fourier-product bounds, asymmetric J estimate, H^1 algebra, unitarity/continuity and complete two-endpoint normal form. Continuous piecewise smooth paths and the exact J(B,.)=C identity are stated with their domains; the proof does not commute an inverse derivative through a product.

R007/S001-S003 gives fixed-tau L^2 continuity of every term of the actual update, smooth finite iterates, endpoint matching of V, and the full a.e. residual formula. The reality clause is correctly conditional on real initial data, while the mean-zero identities also cover complex inputs.

R008/S001-S005 proves every displayed stage, quadratic correction, W, inverse-derivative Y/Y', strong Y and X/negative-norm clause. The final export includes the extra tau in the weak Y norm needed by R009/R010, with constants uniform in support and no numerical Sobolev bound.

R009/S001-S003 proves both stepwise residual bounds and the three interval estimates, explicitly allowing a partial final step. Constant dependence on only M,gamma,T is now stated; the complete residual increments and weak derivative bound are available to R010.

R010/S001-S005 proves exactly the exported interval inequality with N^2*h, h+tau, N^(-1) and N^(-pstar) terms. The proof preserves both boundary terms and estimates the actual forcing via stepwise residuals; the output permits nonzero e(a) and an interval ending inside a step.

R011/S001-S004 chooses all constants from the uniform exact-flow ball and interval inequality, then performs the finite-block recurrence and closes the continuous bootstrap. Explicit L4 supplies tau<=tau0 for the first-hit argument. The export uniformly covers every smooth datum in the ball and all permitted L, independently of higher norms.

R012/S001-S003 chooses C,tau0 from the smooth uniform theorem before u0,L, uses norm-contracting real mean-zero Fourier truncations, the explicit uniform exact L^2 comparison and fixed-tau continuity of the unchanged map for finitely many steps. The finite grid maximum passes to the limit with the same constants. The unique exact-solution convention, normalization, gamma=1 endpoint and full initial-ball uniformity match the frozen target.
